in_hebrew.name: ליסי
in_hebrew.long_meaning: This name is derived from the Hebrew root 'sah' (to bind, to confirm) and 'yatam' (oath, covenant). It means 'God is my oath' or 'God has confirmed my vow'. In the Bible, this name is not found, but it could be a derivative of other Hebrew names such as Leah or Elisheba.

in_greek.name: Λισσή
in_greek.long_meaning: This name is of uncertain origin in Greek. It could be derived from the Greek word 'lissos' (smooth, sleek), in which case it would mean 'smooth one' or 'little one'. Alternatively, it could be derived from the name 'Lysia' (lysos, liberator), in which case it would mean 'liberator' or 'deliverer'. In the Bible, there is no character named Lissi.

in_latin.name: Lissa
in_latin.long_meaning: This name is derived from the Latin word 'lissa' (smooth, plain), and it means 'plain' or 'smooth'. In the Bible, there is no character named Lissa.
